title: Back-to-back measles deaths is our new reality; US tally now at 14
gist: With the US having formally lost measles-elimination status, 2026 cases near 6,000 (highest since 1991) with 14 deaths, outbreaks in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin, and MMR kindergarten coverage at 92.4% versus the 95% herd threshold, Mole argues back-to-back deaths are the new reality.

insights.claim: International health authorities formally declared that the US lost its measles-elimination status in November 2026, meaning measles is again endemic.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Ongoing public-health burden and policy debate around vaccines.

insights.claim: US measles cases in 2026 neared 6,000, the highest count since 1991, across 47 states and jurisdictions, with 43 outbreaks accounting for 96 percent of cases, nearly 650 hospitalizations and 14 deaths.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Scale of resurgence indicates sustained healthcare costs and public-health spending pressure.
insights.locator: The national tally of measles cases

insights.claim: Pennsylvania leads US measles cases with 1,638 and nine deaths and its outbreak appears past peak, while Wisconsin is mid-outbreak with 920 cases, 418 since the start of November.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Geographic hotspots shift; watch Wisconsin trajectory.
insights.locator: In Pennsylvania, which has the record

insights.claim: Only 92.4 percent of US kindergartners received the MMR vaccine in the 2025–2026 school year, below the 95 percent needed to prevent measles footholds, and only 10 states meet that threshold.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Declining vaccination drives the resurgence; a structural rather than transient trend.
insights.locator: To keep measles from getting a foothold

insights.claim: Because measles is the most contagious known virus—lingering in air up to two hours and infecting up to 90 percent of exposed non-immune people—slipping vaccination rates steadily grow the susceptible population.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Expect continued outbreaks absent a reversal in vaccine uptake.

insights.claim: Measles causes 'immune amnesia' by destroying memory immune cells; a 2019 study estimated it erases up to 73 percent of a person's antibody repertoire, leaving survivors vulnerable to other infections.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Hidden downstream disease burden extends costs beyond acute measles cases.

insights.claim: Measles survivors face risk of subacute sclerosing panencephalitis, a rare, fatal neurological disease that can strike years after apparent recovery.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Long-tail health consequences of the outbreak will surface for years.
